claims.text: High-pressure torsion, minor tungsten addition, and annealing at approximately 600°C for 1 hour will produce a nanostructured grain interior in Al0.3CoCrFeNi.
The intervention will produce tungsten-enriched grain boundaries.
The tungsten-enriched grain-boundary network will remain stable at approximately 600°C under sustained load.
Grain refinement will increase strength through the Hall–Petch effect.
Tungsten segregation at grain boundaries will inhibit grain-boundary sliding.
Inhibition of grain-boundary sliding by tungsten segregation will reduce creep.
The treated alloy will exhibit a 15–25% increase in yield strength relative to coarse-grained Al0.3CoCrFeNi without severe plastic deformation or tungsten addition.
The treated alloy will exhibit a lower creep rate at approximately 600°C than the coarse-grained baseline.
The predicted improvements are expected under sustained mechanical load at temperatures around 600°C.
The predicted improvements may not persist at temperatures significantly above 600°C.
The predicted improvements may not transfer to alloy systems other than Al0.3CoCrFeNi.
The uniformity and long-term service stability of tungsten segregation are uncertain.
